Competition Winners!
Dear Mandeville School Gardening Team
We would like to extend our heartfelt congratulations for your participation in the Cultivating Ealing School Gardening Competition 2024.
Your dedication and hard work have truly paid off, earning you the prestigious awards:
Best Sensory Garden
This is an outstanding achievement, building on your previous successes in the competition.
We are thrilled to recognise the continued care and attention you’ve devoted to your gardening programme through establishing a wonderful new garden area. The results are a true testament to your commitment, and it has been a joy to witness your gardening programme flourish. Well done!
Below, you will find feedback from this year’s competition along with suggestions and tips for the 2024/25 gardening season. We hope these insights will inspire even greater success in the future. Warmest congratulations once again—we are excited to stay in touch and follow your garden's continued success throughout the upcoming academic year.
The Cultivating Ealing Team
Cultivating Ealing School Gardening Competition
Highlights Appreciated by the Judges:
1. A beautifully maintained garden brimming with sensory elements—touch, sight, sound, and smell—that creates a serene and engaging learning environment.
2. Vibrant use of colour that adds visual appeal and energy to the garden.
3. Excellent selection of flowers contributing to the garden’s aesthetic.
4. Creative display of national flower images for International Week.
5. Planting spring bulbs for use in the garden and for special events like Mother’s Day.
6. Well-organised garden management with impressive plans and proactive ideas for the upcoming year.
7. Water play features that enhance the garden experience.
8. Innovative banana composting practices.
9. Creative recycling and upcycling efforts that enrich the garden space.
10. Increased involvement of the school community, including parents in donations and plant sales.
11. Effective labelling and signage that enhances the educational value of the garden.

Curriculum, Assessment & Outcomes
At Mandeville, our children are at an early stage of development. To support their learning, we have implemented the early years framework across the school.
We have created a tailored curriculum that covers the seven areas of learning outlined in the SEND Code of Practice and the EYFS framework.
Our curriculum has been developed with input from our school physiotherapist, speech and language therapists, occupational therapists, and music therapists. All staff at Mandeville have the chance to contribute to the ongoing development of the curriculum.
Mandeville Curriculum 1 - Supports children who are working at the engagement levels of learning. The 5 areas of engagement include Exploration, Realisation, Anticipation, Persistence and Initiation.
Mandeville Curriculum 2 - Supports children who are working on ‘I can’ statements and accessing Pre-key stage standards of learning.

Mandeville Nursery
All nursery pupils are referred to Mandeville through the Ealing Early Years Placement Panel. Their families are supported through the Early Help Assessment Plan (EHAP) and Education Health and Care Plan (EHCP) application processes.
The nursery provides a physical and emotionally enabled environment that promotes learning in all Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) areas of the curriculum. The environment also aims to support children in extending their play skills by incorporating each child’s schemas.
The nursery is the first step for many children where routines are embedded and activities are focussed on promoting independence and communication. Daily routines in the nursery consist of short small group structured learning sessions with child-led play sessions in between to ensure a regulated and sensory integrated and balanced routine. Children are encouraged to extend their learning through floor play activities alongside adults modelling play or being a play partner.
Teaching staff in the nursery integrate prescribed therapies into each child’s day to day learning. Therapies include Speech and Language therapy, Occupational therapy, Physiotherapy and recommendations from clinical psychologist.

pageCache.text:
Mandeville satellite is now officially open!
Our new satellite at Oldfield Primary school is an exciting opportunity to provide high quality education for 24 reception and year one children. The provision opened officially on 5th September 2024 and has; three classrooms, a multi-use room, sensory room, and outdoor learning areas. Also each classroom has a calming sensory space and a hygiene area attached to the main room. Classes are also timetabled to use our specialist spa pool at the main Mandeville site.
The Kings Representative Richard Kornicki Esq OBE DL joined us for our celebrations on the 25th September. He was very impressed with the facilities and enjoyed speaking with all the staff about their role in school.
John Burgess, Chair of Governors for Mandeville School, has been involved in the satellite project from the start and has a very strong commitment to providing high quality provision and best practice at Mandeville.
James MacCormack, Headteacher Oldfield Primary School and his staff team have made us feel so welcome on their site. Relationships between Mandeville and Oldfield have gone from strength to strength and we are exploring more ways of working together.
Tsu Pin Huang is our Assistant Head Teacher leading the satellite provision. He is committed to embedding the Mandeville values and expanding the reach of our school community.
The project teams and staff teams have worked very hard to create a stimulating and inviting learning environment for the children ..... watch this space - we are excited about the way forward!

Open Mornings
We have open mornings on the last Thursday and Friday of every month (except if they fall in half-term).
The open mornings give parents an opportunity to visit school, have a tour of some classrooms and resource areas and speak with a member of the senior leadership team. It is a relaxed morning where parents are welcome to ask questions about our provision, share information about their child's needs and meet other children and staff.
Please call reception to book a place. If you wish to be accompanied by another professional (e.g. Keyworker from the nursery), then just let us know when you book.
